newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Chairman of Israel's Bezeq quits.
newsitem.headline: Chairman of Israel's Bezeq quits.

text.p: The chairman of Bezeq Israel Telecom resigned on Wednesday after two-and-a-half years in the post, a spokeswoman said, citing personal reasons for the step.
"Gurion Meltzer notified the Minister of Communications and members of the board of directors that he has decided to resign from his position," the company said in a statement.
A Bezek spokeswoman said Meltzer, appointed in late 1994, was "resigning for personal reasons" which had nothing to do with organisational changes the company was facing.
His resignation would take effect on June 15.

Bezeq, Israel's main telecommunication carrier, has said it will have to undergo restructuring as the government moves to whittle down its decades-old monopoly over communications the country's services.
Last month Israel's ministerial privatisation committee approved a plan to sell 25 percent of Bezeq, reducing its holdings to 51 percent by the end of the year.
The Israeli government currently holds 76 percent of Bezeq. The rest trades on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, although about half the float is controlled by Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc.
